page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The server does not include a GPU and comes with 33 GB of local storage, with support for Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are strong, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the top 25% at 2707.07. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with both small-block cached read-only and large-block uncached read/write operations scoring in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic performance is average, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D4as_v4 offers a stable entry-level resource profile for general-purpose workloads. Its single-core performance makes it suitable for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and simple text processing. However, due to weak multi-core scaling, low memory bandwidth, and low database operation scores, it is less suited for heavy database workloads, parallel software compilation, or multi-threaded data processing.
